name: Gen Digital Inc.
moat_justification: Norton, Avast and LifeLock give Gen the leading consumer cyber-safety subscription franchise — brand trust, OEM/partner distribution and high retention in a category where the product is bought on fear of loss — but the core antivirus product commoditizes against free platform offerings (Microsoft Defender, Apple/Google built-ins), switching costs are low, and MoneyLion's marketplace is a competitive lead-gen business with no real moat. Returns evidence caps the score: post-Avast roic_proxy ran 8.5% (FY23), 8.9% (FY24), 10.6% (FY25), 13.1% (FY26) — improving but only around the cost of capital on the acquisition-swollen capital base, versus 33-47% in FY21-22 pre-Avast. Gross margin is high but eroding with mix: 85.4% (FY22) to 78.5% (FY26), TTM 78.0%, as lower-margin MoneyLion revenue scales. A 5 = narrow moat, CAP 8.5 years.
fragility_flags: OE_VOLATILE: OE/share range over the last 5 yrs spans >3x — normalized base helps but the business is cyclical; widen bear weight
NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE: net income and operating cash flow differ by >40% in 2024, 2025 — find the one-off (tax deposits, impairments, WC swings) before trusting the OE base
WIDE_SCENARIO_SPREAD: super-bull IV is 4.5x super-bear IV — uncertainty is huge; confidence should not be high
HIGH_NET_DEBT: net debt is 5.7x normalized OE — levered OE can vanish fast; stress the bear cases
TIER_BAND: bear-case tier C (12.3%) vs bull-case tier A (20.2%) — the verdict spans tiers; size any position to the bear end
one_liner: Durable consumer cyber-safety subscription franchise plus fast-growing MoneyLion, but a narrow 5/10 moat and net debt at 5.7x normalized OE; weighted IRR 15.8% only just clears the 15% hurdle at $24.16 (weighted IV@15% $25.88) with the price still carrying a GoDaddy-deal discount — size to the bear end (12.3%); it clears 15% with real margin only below ~$20.
moat_for: Category-leading consumer brands (Norton, Avast, LifeLock) in subscription cyber safety with high retention
Distribution scale: OEM, ISP and retail partner channels plus ~110M connected financial accounts via MoneyLion
Recurring subscription revenue with 50%+ non-GAAP operating margins in Cyber Safety (61% segment margin Q1 FY27)
Cross-sell platform: 35% of paid customers now use financial-wellness tools, deepening engagement
moat_against: Free platform competition: Microsoft Defender and Apple/Google built-in security commoditize core antivirus
Low switching costs and a mature, slow-growing consumer AV category
ROIC only ~9-13% post-Avast — the rollup capital base has not yet earned a wide-moat return
Gross margin drifting down (85.4% FY22 to 78.5% FY26) as no-moat MoneyLion marketplace mix grows
Growth-by-acquisition model: Avast, MoneyLion, and a reported GoDaddy approach — moat is bought, not organic
